families.product_name: QLAB Advanced Quantification Software: 3D Auto RV and 3D Auto MV
families.summary: QLAB Q-Apps 3D Auto RV (QLAB 13.0, K191647) and 3D Auto MV (QLAB 15.0, K200974) combine the machine-learning segmentation engine of Philips HeartModel (K181264) with TOMTEC-Arena 4D RV-Function and 4D MV-Assessment (K150122) to produce editable 3D surface models and measurements of the right ventricle and mitral valve from 3D echocardiography. QLAB runs on a standard PC, a dedicated workstation, or on-board Philips ultrasound systems. The FDA summary for 3D Auto RV reports RMSE versus the predicate 4D RV of 8.3 mL (EDV), 2.7 mL (ESV) and 2.7% (EF); the 3D Auto MV summary reports no quantitative metrics.
families.intended_use_quote: QLAB Advanced Quantification Software is a software application package. It is designed to view and quantify image data acquired on Philips ultrasound systems.
families.indications_for_use_quote: QLAB Advanced Quantification Software is a software application package. It is designed to view and quantify image data acquired on Philips ultrasound systems.
embedded_ai_features: 3D Auto RV: machine-learning auto-segmentation (HeartModel engine applied to the RV) integrated with TOMTEC-Arena 4D RV-Function; 3D surface model created semi-automatically without user interaction, user edits/accepts/rejects contours; outputs EDV, EDVI, ESV, ESVI, SV, EF plus 2D RVD1-3, TAPSE, FAC, RVLS (free wall, septum)

3D Auto MV: machine-learning-derived HeartModel segmentation engine integrated with TOMTEC-Arena TTA2 4D MV-Assessment; provides initial mitral-valve landmark proposals then annulus/leaflet/tenting/coaptation measurements; adds D-shaped annulus perimeter/area, maximum prolapse height, maximum open coaptation gap/width, total open coaptation area versus the reference device

clearances.changes_summary: Adds the 3D Auto RV Q-App to QLAB 13.0: integrates the HeartModel (K181264) machine-learning segmentation engine, applied to the right ventricle, with the TomTec-Arena 4D RV-Function (reference device K150122). Predicate HeartModel had no RV parameters; 3D RV EDV measurement gains a semi-automatic function, all other RV measurements identical to 4D RV. Algorithm training procedure stated to be the same as HeartModel except applied to the RV.

Adds the 3D Auto MV Q-App to QLAB 15.0: integrates the HeartModel machine-learning segmentation engine (applied to the mitral valve) with the TomTec-Arena TTA2 4D MV-Assessment application (reference K150122). Introduces D-Shaped Annulus Perimeter, D-Shaped Annulus Area, Maximum Prolapse Height, Maximum Open Coaptation Gap/Width and Total Open Coaptation Area; all other measurements identical to 4D MV-Assessment. Indications unchanged.
notable_flags: no quantitative performance metrics in summary

performance_claims.endpoint: RV end-diastolic volume error vs predicate 4D RV
performance_claims.value: below 15% for every data set tested
performance_claims.dataset_description: Validation study; test datasets segregated from training data sets; n not stated
performance_claims.quote: The results of a validation study show that the overall performance of the 3D Auto RV software generates RV end diastolic volume error rates below 15% for every data set tested compared to the predicate 4D RV.

performance_claims.endpoint: RV end-diastolic volume agreement vs predicate 4D RV
performance_claims.dataset_description: Validation study; test datasets segregated from training data sets; n not stated
performance_claims.quote: A root mean square error (RMSE) analysis showed that in comparison to the predicate 4D RV, 3D Auto RV measured end diastolic RV volumes with 8.3 ml RMSE, end systolic RV volumes with 2.7 ml RMSE, and RV ejection fraction with 2.7% RMSE. Test datasets were segregated from training data sets.

performance_claims.endpoint: RV end-systolic volume agreement vs predicate 4D RV
performance_claims.dataset_description: Validation study; test datasets segregated from training data sets; n not stated
performance_claims.quote: 3D Auto RV measured end diastolic RV volumes with 8.3 ml RMSE, end systolic RV volumes with 2.7 ml RMSE, and RV ejection fraction with 2.7% RMSE.

performance_claims.endpoint: RV ejection fraction agreement vs predicate 4D RV
performance_claims.dataset_description: Validation study; test datasets segregated from training data sets; n not stated
performance_claims.quote: 3D Auto RV measured end diastolic RV volumes with 8.3 ml RMSE, end systolic RV volumes with 2.7 ml RMSE, and RV ejection fraction with 2.7% RMSE.

performance_claims.endpoint: External study (JASE) - proportion of patients needing no contour revision; RV volume difference vs CMR
performance_claims.metric: % needing no revision; % difference vs CMR
performance_claims.value: no revision in one-third of patients; all 3D Auto RV results <15% difference from CMR RV volume
performance_claims.dataset_description: External published study in JASE (not named in summary; consistent with Genovese et al. 2019, n=56)
performance_claims.quote: An external study published in the Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography which concludes that 3D Auto RV provides an accurate and highly reproducible quantification not needing any revision in one-third of patients and needing only minor revisions in the rest of patients. The users were able to discern the patients images which needed manual editing on all cases. Ground truth in this study was considered to be the cross-modality CMR. 3D Auto RV results all showed less than 15% difference from the CMR measurements of RV volume.

performance_claims.endpoint: 3D Auto RV auto-segmentation EDV vs expert manual adjustment (Philips/TOMTEC white paper)
performance_claims.value: R = 0.79; 65% of data sets within 15%, 49% within 10% of manual
performance_claims.comparator: Expert manual adjustment of image alignment and contour position
performance_claims.quote: EDV results from the auto-segmentation were compared to expert manual adjustment of the image alignment and contour position for 73 data sets. Shown in Figure 5 is the correlation plot of the EDV for the auto-segmentation versus the manual adjustments for the 73 data sets. The R-value is 0.79. For 65% of the data sets, the EDV from the auto-segmentation were within 15% of the manual adjustments, and for 49% of the data sets the automatic results were within 10% of the manual results.

performance_claims.endpoint: ML-based 3D RV volumes/EF vs CMR after minimal editing (Genovese 2019, JASE)
performance_claims.value: EDV bias -25.6 +/- 21.1 mL; ESV -7.4 +/- 16 mL; EF -3.3% +/- 5.2%; fully automatic accurate in 32% (15 +/- 1 s), editing needed in 68% (114 +/- 71 s); CoV <7%, ICC >=0.95
performance_claims.dataset_description: 56 unselected patients referred for clinically indicated CMR with same-day 3DE; wide range of RV size, function and image quality
performance_claims.quote: With these minimal adjustments, RV volumes and EF measurements were accurate in comparison with CMR reference (biases: EDV, -25.6 +/- 21.1 mL; ESV, -7.4 +/- 16 mL; EF, -3.3% +/- 5.2%) and showed excellent reproducibility reflected by coefficients of variation <7% and intraclass correlations >=0.95 for all measurements.

performance_claims.endpoint: Fully automated 3D RV software vs CMR and semi-automated TomTec (Otani 2020, EHJ-CVI)
performance_claims.value: feasibility 91%; EDV bias -12.6 mL (r=0.82); SV bias -5.1 mL (r=0.78); RVEF no significant difference (r=0.72); analysis 15 s vs 120 s
performance_claims.comparator: Cardiac magnetic resonance; semi-automated TomTec software
performance_claims.quote: Although the fully automated software, without any manual editing, significantly underestimated RV end-diastolic volume (bias: -12.6 mL, P < 0.001) and stroke volume (-5.1 mL, P < 0.001) compared with CMR, there were good correlations between the two modalities (r = 0.82 and 0.78). No significant differences in RVEF between the fully automated software and CMR were observed, and there was a fair correlation (r = 0.72).

performance_claims.endpoint: Fully automated 3DE RV software in children vs CMR (Liu 2025, Pediatr Radiol)
performance_claims.value: feasible in 100%; fully automated in 35% (8 +/- 2 s); RVEDV r=0.93, RVESV r=0.90, RVEF r=0.82
performance_claims.dataset_description: 82 prospectively enrolled children with echo and cardiac MR within 24 h
performance_claims.subgroup_notes: Bias smaller in children with RVEF >=45%, normal RV size and good 3DE image quality
performance_claims.quote: The 3DE-derived RV volumes and EF correlated well with cardiac MR measurements (RVEDV, r=0.93; RVESV, r=0.90; RVEF, r=0.82; all P <0.001).

performance_claims.endpoint: Real-world feasibility of 3D Auto RV semi-automated analysis (Shiokawa 2026, J Echocardiogr)
performance_claims.metric: feasibility; % fully automated; analysis time reduction
performance_claims.value: feasibility 84.8% (201/237) of 3D datasets, 67.4% (201/298) of consecutive patients; fully automated without correction 10.9% (22/201); 30% shorter analysis time vs manual 2D
performance_claims.dataset_description: 201 patients with 2D and 3D TTE, July-November 2023, routine clinical practice
performance_claims.quote: The feasibility of RV measurement using the AI-based software was 84.8% (201/237) among patients with available 3D datasets, and the overall applicability was 67.4% (201/298) across all consecutive patients undergoing routine echocardiography. Among the 201 analyzed cases, fully automated analysis without manual correction was feasible in 10.9% (22/201), while the remaining 89.1% required manual adjustments of the endocardial borders to ensure clinical accuracy.

training_data.description: FDA summaries state only that non-clinical V&V included 'Machine Learning Algorithm Training and the subsequent Validation Study' (K191647 p.8; K200974 p.11) and that the training procedure is the same as the predicate HeartModel, applied to the RV / MV instead of the LV. No training-set size, site count or population is given. Philips/TOMTEC white paper (company) states the boundary detector and shape models 'are trained using a large number of clinical images annotated by echocardiographic experts'.
training_data.source: K191647.txt p.7-8; K200974.txt p.8-9, 11; Philips 3D Auto RV white paper (4522 991 48031, Apr 2019)

validation_data.description: K191647: internal validation study versus predicate 4D RV with test datasets 'segregated from training data sets'; n not stated. Plus an external JASE study versus CMR (consistent with Genovese 2019, n=56). Company white paper: 73 data sets auto-segmentation vs expert manual adjustment. K200974: 'Algorithm Training and the subsequent Validation Study' for 3D Auto MV, no numbers.
validation_data.source: K191647.txt p.8; K200974.txt p.11; Philips white paper p.5

prior_validations.description: Philips press release 20 June 2019 (EPIQ CVx Release 5.0, ASE 2019): '3D Auto RV application segments, identifies the borders of and aligns the views of the right ventricle, enabling clinicians to carry out the quantification and check the measurements in as little as 15 seconds'; 'designed using a Machine Learning-based algorithm, is CE marked and FDA 510(k) pending'.

Philips/TOMTEC white paper '3D Auto RV - right ventricular quantification' (Sedlmeier, Prater; Apr 2019): deformable-model auto-segmentation (boundary detector + RV shape models, AI-trained, speckle-tracked over cycle); EDV auto vs manual in 73 data sets, R=0.79, 65% within 15%; on-cart and off-cart results identical; requires >=10 volumes/s and >=10 volumes/cycle; no validation for contrast data.

Predicate HeartModel segmentation engine validated in Tsang 2016 (n=159, vs manual 3D and CMR) and multicentre Medvedofsky 2018 (n=180, 6 sites); the K191647/K200974 summaries state the training procedure is the same as HeartModel.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Three-Dimensional Echocardiographic Quantification of Right Ventricular Size and Function: Validation Against Cardiac Magnetic Resonance
papers.key_result: Fully automatic results accurate in 32% (15 +/- 1 s); after minimal editing biases vs CMR: EDV -25.6 +/- 21.1 mL, ESV -7.4 +/- 16 mL, EF -3.3% +/- 5.2%; ICC >=0.95. Matches the 'external study published in JASE' cited in the K191647 summary.

papers.title: Accuracy of fully automated right ventricular quantification software with 3D echocardiography: direct comparison with cardiac magnetic resonance and semi-automated quantification software
papers.key_result: Feasibility 91%; fully automated software underestimated RVEDV (bias -12.6 mL, r=0.82) and SV (-5.1 mL) vs CMR; RVEF not significantly different (r=0.72); analysis 15 s vs 120 s for semi-automated TomTec.

papers.title: Feasibility and Accuracy of a Fully Automated Right Ventricular Quantification Software With Three-Dimensional Echocardiography: Comparison With Cardiac Magnetic Resonance

Quantification of chronic aortic regurgitation using left and right ventricular stroke volumes obtained from two new automated three-dimensional transthoracic echocardiographic software: feasibility and accuracy
papers.key_result: Dynamic HeartModel + 3D Auto RV regurgitant volume correlated with RT3DE reference (central r=0.90, eccentric r=0.96); kappa for grading 0.89/0.86.

papers.title: Feasibility and accuracy of the fully automated three-dimensional echocardiography right ventricular quantification software in children: validation against cardiac magnetic resonance
papers.key_result: Feasible in 100% of 82 children; fully automated in 35% (8 +/- 2 s); RVEDV r=0.93, RVESV r=0.90, RVEF r=0.82 vs cardiac MR; volumes slightly underestimated, RVEF overestimated.

papers.title: Agreement of AI-assisted semi-automated right ventricular function analysis using 3D transthoracic echocardiography with artificial intelligence
papers.key_result: 3D Auto RV feasible in 84.8% of 3D datasets (67.4% of consecutive patients); fully automated without correction in 10.9%; analysis time 30% shorter than manual 2D.

papers.title: Transthoracic 3D Echocardiographic Left Heart Chamber Quantification Using an Automated Adaptive Analytics Algorithm
papers.key_result: Validation of the predicate HeartModel segmentation engine (whose training procedure the 3D Auto RV/MV summaries cite): r=0.87-0.96 vs manual 3D TTE, r=0.84-0.95 vs CMR.

papers.title: Three-dimensional echocardiographic quantification of the left-heart chambers using an automated adaptive analytics algorithm: multicentre validation study
papers.key_result: Multicentre (6 sites) validation of predicate HeartModel: r 0.97 (LVEDV), 0.97 (LVESV), 0.88 (LVEF), 0.96 (LAV) vs core-lab manual tracing.

open_questions: Training-set size, number of sites and patient mix for the 3D Auto RV and 3D Auto MV machine-learning models are not stated in K191647 or K200974 (only 'Machine Learning Algorithm Training and the subsequent Validation Study'); the white paper says 'a large number of clinical images' without a number.
Sample size, site count and patient characteristics of the K191647 internal validation study (RMSE 8.3 mL / 2.7 mL / 2.7%) are not stated.

K200974 (3D Auto MV) reports no quantitative performance metrics at all ('meets the defined requirements and performance claims'); the 3D Auto MV validation study n, comparator and results are unknown.

No peer-reviewed publication specifically validating the Philips 3D Auto MV Q-App (K200974) was found on PubMed with the terms tried ('3D Auto MV', automated mitral valve + QLAB/HeartModel); earlier Philips automated MV papers (e.g., Aquila 2016, Cardiovasc Ultrasound) concern a prior 'anatomical intelligence' MV tool and were not attributed to this clearance.
The JASE external study in the K191647 summary is unnamed; attribution to Genovese et al. 2019 is inferred from the matching journal, one-third-no-revision finding and CMR ground truth.
Ahmad 2021 (Front Cardiovasc Med) abstract was not retrieved in this session; n_subjects and key result left null.
The 3D Auto RV white paper's 73-data-set validation (R=0.79) is a company document; it is unclear whether this is the same dataset as the FDA validation study.
openFDA applicant is 'Philips Health Care'; the 510(k) summaries name Philips Ultrasound, Inc. (Andover MA / Bothell WA).

families.product_name: CARTOSOUND FAM Module (CARTO 3 EP Navigation System)
families.summary: CARTOSOUND FAM is a deep-learning module of the CARTO 3 EP Navigation System (V8.0, K231207) that automatically reconstructs an editable 3D left-atrial volume with automatic 3D segmentation from gated 2D intracardiac-echo frames acquired from the right atrium and/or RVOT. V8.1 (K252302) carries the CARTOSOUND FAM LA module forward with SOUNDSTAR Crystal catheter support; V8.4 (K252972, cleared with a PCCP) retires the legacy FAM module and replaces it with the locked-AI CARTOSOUND REVEAL module for LA and LV ultrasound mapping. The FDA summaries report no quantitative accuracy metrics for the AI segmentation.
families.intended_use_quote: The intended use of the CARTO™ 3 System is catheter-based cardiac electrophysiological (EP) procedures. The CARTO™ 3 System provides information about the electrical activity of the heart and about catheter location during the procedure. The system can be used on patients who are eligible for a conventional electrophysiological procedure. The system has no special contraindications.
families.indications_for_use_quote: The intended use of the CARTO™ 3 System is catheter-based cardiac electrophysiological (EP) procedures. The CARTO™ 3 System provides information about the electrical activity of the heart and about catheter location during the procedure. The system can be used on patients who are eligible for a conventional electrophysiological procedure. The system has no special contraindications.
embedded_ai_features: CARTOSOUND FAM (V8.0): deep-learning automatic 3D segmentation and reconstruction of the left atrium from a series of 2D ultrasound gated input frames acquired from the RA (fossa ovalis) and/or RVOT
Complex Signals Identification (V8.0): machine-learning locked algorithm tagging fractionated intracardiac EGMs (not an ultrasound feature)

CARTOSOUND REVEAL (V8.4): locked AI algorithms for automatic identification of cardiac structures on ICE images, automatic 2D contours, and automatic 3D shell creation for LA and LV reconstruction; replaces legacy CARTOSOUND FAM
LA FAM Module (V8.4): locked AI algorithm generating a 3D LA shell when mapping with the VARIPULSE catheter (not ultrasound-based)

clearances.changes_summary: CARTO 3 V8.0 vs V7.4 (K223733): adds Multipolar Mapping, Auto Pattern Acquisition, Complex Signals Identification (locked ML algorithm), CARTOSOUND FAM (deep-learning automatic 3D LA segmentation/reconstruction from gated 2D ICE frames), LAT Velocity Vectors, catheter support (QDOT Micro improvements, OPTRELL, LASSOSTAR NAV), and legacy modifications (Compensated VISITAG stability, Late Annotation Mapping, CONFIDENSE SmartMap). Hardware unchanged; indications unchanged.
notable_flags: real-world evidence (REAL AF Registry sub-study, zero/low fluoroscopy)

clearances.changes_summary: CARTO 3 V8.1 vs V8.0: adds FARAWAVE catheter visualization with Tissue Proximity Indication, VARIPULSE catheter / TRUPULSE generator PFA support, and SOUNDSTAR Crystal ultrasound catheter support ('compatible with the legacy CARTO 3 CARTOSOUND SW and CARTOSOUND FAM LA Modules'); minor enhancements to legacy features including CARTOSOUND 4D and CARTOSOUND FAM LA. Retrospective validation on historic EP procedure data and animal testing.

CARTO 3 V8.4 vs V8.1: 'The legacy CARTOSOUND FAM Module is not supported in CARTO 3 EP Navigation System V8.4., as its functionality has been replaced with CARTOSOUND REVEAL.' Adds CARTOSOUND REVEAL (locked AI for automatic identification of cardiac structures on ICE images, automatic 2D contours and automatic 3D shell creation for LA and LV; supports SOUNDSTAR family and NUVISION NAV catheters) and LA FAM Module (locked AI 3D LA shell when mapping with VARIPULSE). PCCP covers additional retraining datasets, AI model optimizations, additional anatomical structures in REVEAL, additional LA FAM input devices, map coloring, and external-device information display.

performance_claims.endpoint: CARTOSOUND FAM LA reconstruction vs cardiac CT (Di Biase 2023, Europace)
performance_claims.metric: calculation time; correlation of ostial diameters / carina-to-carina distance
performance_claims.value: mean LA reconstruction 65 s; ostial diameters and carina-to-carina distance comparable to CT (no significant difference), r = 0.52-0.75 except RIPV r = 0.20
performance_claims.comparator: Cardiac computed tomography; three independent electrophysiologists' qualitative rating
performance_claims.dataset_description: 28 patients undergoing AF ablation; 3D shells of LA body, LAA and four PVs generated by the DL algorithm from ICE frames gated to end-expiration and max LA volume
performance_claims.quote: Average calculation time for LA reconstruction was 65 s. Mean ostial diameters and carina-to-carina distance were all comparable to CT without statistical significance. Ostial diameters and carina-to-carina distance also showed moderate to high correlation (r = 0.52-0.75) except for RIPV (r = 0.20).

performance_claims.endpoint: AI-assisted ICE mapping (CARTOSOUND FAM) vs conventional EAM during pulsed field ablation (Dello Russo 2025, J Clin Med)
performance_claims.metric: median LA mapping time; LA dwell time; fluoroscopy time; feasibility
performance_claims.value: feasible in all cases; LA mapping time 5 vs 8 min (p<0.001); LA dwell time 33.5 vs 38.5 min (p=0.001); fluoroscopy 7.5 vs 14 min (p<0.001); no major adverse events
performance_claims.dataset_description: Retrospective multicenter study; 157 consecutive PFA patients (64 ICE-guided, 93 non-ICE-guided), paroxysmal or persistent AF
performance_claims.quote: AI-assisted ICE mapping was feasible in all cases. Compared with conventional mapping, it significantly reduced LA (left atrium) mapping time (median 5 vs. 8 min; p < 0.001), LA dwell time (33.5 vs. 38.5 min; p = 0.001), and fluoroscopy time (7.5 vs. 14 min; p < 0.001).

performance_claims.endpoint: AI FAM vs standard-of-care EAM in RF AF ablation, 1-year outcomes (Zou 2026, Europace)
performance_claims.metric: procedure time; LA dwell time; acute success; freedom from AF at 1 year
performance_claims.value: procedure time 122.5 +/- 23.5 vs 129.0 +/- 30.4 min (P=0.040); LA dwell 78.3 +/- 21.45 vs 87.5 +/- 28.2 min (P=0.001); acute success 98.3% vs 98.9%; complications 1 vs 4; 1-year freedom from AF 80.0% vs 81.4% (P=0.610)
performance_claims.dataset_description: 298 RF AF ablation patients Jan 2021-Dec 2023; 115 AI FAM (2023) vs 183 EAM (before 2023)
performance_claims.quote: AI FAM reduced mean total procedure time (122.5 +/- 23.5 vs. 129.0 +/- 30.4 min, P = 0.040) and left atrial (LA) dwell time (78.3 +/- 21.45 vs. 87.5 +/- 28.2 min, P = 0.001). Acute procedural success was 98.3% in AI FAM vs. 98.9% in EAM with fewer complications observed in the AI FAM group (1 vs. 4). At 1 year, freedom from AF recurrence was comparable (80.0% AI FAM vs. 81.4% EAM at 1 year, LogRank P = 0.610).

performance_claims.endpoint: AIFAM-guided no-pre-mapping PFA with variable loop circular catheter (Zou 2026, Europace)
performance_claims.metric: acute procedural success; complications; arrhythmia-free survival at 270 days
performance_claims.value: acute success 100%; one vascular complication (0.5%); freedom from arrhythmia after 60-day blanking 77.7% (paroxysmal) and 71.8% (non-paroxysmal) at 270 days
performance_claims.dataset_description: 210 of 412 VLCC PFA patients who underwent AIFAM-guided ablation without pre-map; 184 with follow-up
performance_claims.quote: Acute procedural success was achieved in 100% of cases. One acute non-catheter related vascular complication (0.5%) and no late complications were documented. Among 184 patients with at least one follow-up, freedom from arrhythmia survival after 60-day blanking was 77.7% in paroxysmal AF and 71.8% in non-paroxysmal AF at 270 days.

training_data.description: K231207 (p.7): 'The CARTOSOUND FAM Module incorporates a Deep Learning (DL) algorithm. Data for training and validation of the DL algorithm was collected from diverse locations and populations, using a variety of ultrasound system settings, scanners, and Catheters.' No counts. K252972 (p.8) for CARTOSOUND REVEAL: training/validation data 'collected from a representative range of LA and LV chamber volumes and geographical locations, using a variety of ultrasound system settings, ULS scanners, and catheters'; anatomical labeling/contouring algorithms developed and tested on CARTO 3 cases with ultrasound information; 3D shell model developed and tested using CT and CARTO 3 FAM cases. No counts.

validation_data.description: K231207: 'Retrospective Validation Tests - Testing was performed to validate the clinical functionality and quality of new introduced modules. Testing was performed retrospectively, on clinical recorded data from historic EP procedures performed with the CARTO 3 System.' (p.10). Same language in K252302 (p.9) and K252972 (p.9). No sample sizes, sites, or accuracy metrics disclosed; separation of validation data from training data not stated.

prior_validations.description: J&J press release 8 May 2024 (CARTO 3 Version 8 launch): CARTOSOUND FAM is 'the first use of an artificial intelligence algorithm, cleared by the FDA in intracardiac ultrasound for Biosense Webster'; 'automated 3D shell creation using deep-learning technology'; enables 'automatic generation of the left atrial anatomy before inserting the catheter to the left atrium'.

K231207 clinical testing: REAL AF Registry sub-study (real-world evidence) of paroxysmal AF ablation with a zero/low fluoroscopy workflow met primary safety and secondary acute effectiveness endpoints; not specific to CARTOSOUND FAM and no numbers given.

papers.title: Feasibility of three-dimensional artificial intelligence algorithm integration with intracardiac echocardiography for left atrial imaging during atrial fibrillation catheter ablation
papers.key_result: CARTOSOUND FAM DL reconstruction of LA in 65 s; ostial diameters and carina-to-carina distance comparable to CT (r=0.52-0.75, RIPV r=0.20); good qualitative agreement across three electrophysiologists.

papers.title: AI-Assisted 3D Intracardiac Echocardiography for Pulsed Field Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation Using a Novel Variable Loop Circular Catheter: A Multicenter Evaluation
papers.key_result: Retrospective multicenter; AI-assisted ICE mapping feasible in all cases; reduced LA mapping time (5 vs 8 min), LA dwell (33.5 vs 38.5 min) and fluoroscopy time (7.5 vs 14 min) vs conventional mapping; no major adverse events.

papers.title: Atrial fibrillation ablation using three-dimensional artificial intelligence module integration with intracardiac echocardiography
papers.key_result: AI FAM (n=115) vs EAM (n=183): shorter procedure time (122.5 vs 129.0 min) and LA dwell (78.3 vs 87.5 min); acute success 98.3% vs 98.9%; 1-year freedom from AF 80.0% vs 81.4%.

papers.title: AI-ICE Guided Pulsed Field Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation with Variable Loop Circular Catheter
papers.key_result: No-pre-map AIFAM-guided PFA: acute success 100%, 0.5% vascular complication, arrhythmia freedom 77.7% (paroxysmal) / 71.8% (non-paroxysmal) at 270 days.

open_questions: K254085 (CARTO 3 V9.0 with PIU Plus, decided 2026-01-18, Special 510(k), predicate K252302) is EXCLUDED from clearances: its summary describes only the improved Patient Interface Unit (PIU Plus) and supporting software; it never mentions CARTOSOUND FAM, CARTOSOUND REVEAL, deep learning or AI. Because its predicate (V8.1) carried CARTOSOUND FAM LA, the module presumably persists in V9.0, but the summary does not say so.

K252972 (V8.4) is INCLUDED on the basis that its summary explicitly carries the AI ICE segmentation forward under a new name ('The legacy CARTOSOUND FAM Module is not supported ... as its functionality has been replaced with CARTOSOUND REVEAL'); if the registry intends strict module-name continuity, this clearance should instead be filed as the successor product 'CARTOSOUND REVEAL' with a PCCP.
Chronology note: K252972 (received 2025-09-17, decided 2026-02-20) was decided after K254085 (received 2025-12-18, decided 2026-01-18); both cite K252302 as predicate.

No FDA summary in this lineage gives any quantitative accuracy metric for CARTOSOUND FAM or CARTOSOUND REVEAL (e.g., segmentation Dice, volume error vs CT); performance is described only as 'met the acceptance criteria'.

Training and validation dataset sizes, number of sites/countries, catheter types and patient characteristics for the FAM and REVEAL deep-learning models are not disclosed; whether validation data were independent of training is not stated.
K231207 lists both a Complex Signals Identification ML algorithm and CARTOSOUND FAM; only FAM is ultrasound-based and is the subject of this family entry.

The J&J press release (May 2024) cites '91% of cases (n=27)' for identification of critical isthmuses; this appears to relate to CARTO ELEVATE/signal features rather than CARTOSOUND FAM and was not recorded as a FAM performance claim.

Two further PubMed hits mentioning CARTOSOUND FAM/REVEAL were not reviewed in full (Chan WK 2026 PACE how-to article, PMID 41950105; Narita M 2026 J Cardiovasc Electrophysiol on Tissue Proximity Indication, PMID 42378433) and are omitted.
NCT04600245 (Tel Aviv) has not been updated since October 2020; no results posted and no linked publication identified.
Company product page for CARTO 3 software describes only CARTOSOUND FAM (Version 8); no public product page for CARTOSOUND REVEAL (V8.4) was found as of this session.
